faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Common questions, answered up front.
faq.subtitle: If you're evaluating Flyto2 for the team, these are the things people ask first.

items.q: Is Flyto2 really free and open source?
items.a: Yes. The execution engine (`flyto-core`) is MIT-licensed on GitHub. You can install it from PyPI today and run flows without ever creating an account. The hosted cloud is a paid option layered on top — never a requirement.

items.q: How is this different from Zapier or Make?
items.a: Zapier and Make connect SaaS APIs in the cloud. Flyto2 records and replays the actual browser — including sites without a public API — and runs it on your own machine. If your bank, ERP or vendor portal isn't on Zapier's catalog, that's exactly the gap Flyto2 fills.

items.q: What happens when the website I'm automating changes?
items.a: Flyto2 records semantic actions ("click the Login button") rather than fragile CSS selectors. When a site re-skins itself, most flows keep running. When something does break, you pause, fix the one step, and resume — you don't rewrite the whole flow.

items.q: Can my team share workflows?
items.a: Yes. Workflows are plain files you can commit to git, share via the in-app Marketplace, or hand to a colleague over Slack. Run history stays local; only the workflow definition travels.

items.q: What does it cost?
items.a: The desktop app and the open-source engine are free for individual use. Pro and Team tiers add hosted scheduling, shared marketplaces and priority support — pricing is on the Cloud page.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Cloud — questions we hear most.
faq.subtitle: Recording, replay, security, pricing — the answers ops and IT leads ask for before approving a tool.

items.q: Does Cloud work on sites without a public API?
items.a: That's exactly its job. If you can do the task in a browser, Flyto2 can record and replay it — internal portals, government sites, legacy ERPs, anywhere.

items.q: Is it really running on my machine?
items.a: Yes. The desktop app bundles a Chromium engine and the workflow runtime. Your credentials, recorded steps and execution history live on your disk. The cloud is opt-in for scheduling, sharing and team features.

items.q: What happens when a website redesigns?
items.a: Flyto2 records semantic intent ("click Sign in", "fill the email field") rather than brittle XPath. When a site re-skins itself, most flows keep working. When one step breaks, you fix only that step in the visual editor.

items.q: Can I trigger flows from CI / a script?
items.a: Yes. Every workflow has a CLI invocation and a webhook URL. Run them from cron, GitHub Actions, your own backend, or Flyto2's hosted scheduler — same workflow file, same result.

items.q: How do you handle 2FA and CAPTCHAs?
items.a: Flyto2 can pause and prompt you (or a human in your team) to complete a 2FA challenge, then continue. CAPTCHAs are deliberately not bypassed — using Flyto2 on sites that ban automation is your call, not ours.

items.q: What's the pricing?
items.a: Free for individual use of the desktop app and OSS engine. Pro adds hosted scheduling and unlimited cloud runs; Team adds shared marketplace and SSO. Detailed pricing on the Cloud page.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Pricing questions, answered.
faq.subtitle: Compute points, seat limits, billing — the questions buyers ask before they pull out the card.

items.q: What's a "compute point"?
items.a: A point is a unit of work — roughly one workflow step (a click, a CSV row, an API call). 50,000 points covers about 100 hours of typical browser automation per month.

items.q: Is the free plan really free forever?
items.a: Yes. The desktop app and the open-source engine are free for personal use forever. The only thing the free tier doesn't include is hosted scheduling and team features.

items.q: What happens if I exceed monthly points?
items.a: Workflows pause until the next cycle, or you can buy a top-up at $0.20 per 1,000 points. We never silently overcharge — you confirm the top-up before it runs.

items.q: Do you offer annual billing or discounts?
items.a: Annual billing saves 20% on Pro and Team. Education and non-profit discounts available — email info@flyto2.com.

items.q: Can I self-host instead?
items.a: Yes. The OSS engine on PyPI runs everything except hosted scheduling. Enterprise self-host with SSO and air-gapped deploy is on the roadmap.

hero.title: One war room.
hero.lede: SCA, SAST, secret detection, license audit, CVE triage, pentest workflows, runtime telemetry. Warroom is the operating picture for the security of every line of code you ship.

closedLoop.label: WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT
closedLoop.title: Closed-loop verification.
closedLoop.subtitle: Every other security tool stops at the alert. Warroom turns each finding into a YAML pentest, runs it against your staging in a real browser, and reports a verdict — exploit, sanitised, or unreachable.

find.title: Find
find.body: SCA, SAST, secrets, license, IaC. Same scan parses your code into call graphs and architecture maps.

craft.title: Craft
craft.body: For each security-relevant finding, generate a YAML pentest workflow scoped to the affected route.

run.title: Run
run.body: Execute the workflow against staging in a real Chrome session. 12 official OWASP / LLM / business-logic playbooks ship today.

verdictStep.title: Verdict
verdictStep.body: Capture HMAC-signed evidence, report exploitable / sanitized / unreachable, store the workflow in the regression vault for nightly re-runs.

exploitable.title: Exploitable
exploitable.body: The vulnerability runs end-to-end. Evidence pack attached. Triage to top of the queue.

sanitized.title: Sanitized
sanitized.body: Mitigated by a downstream control (auth, WAF, framework). Logged, deprioritised.

unreachable.title: Unreachable
unreachable.body: The vulnerable code exists but no path of user input reaches it. Acknowledged, low priority.

proof.label: REAL PROOF
proof.title: We tested it on OWASP Juice Shop.
proof.subtitle: Not a synthetic sandbox. The classic intentionally-vulnerable e-commerce app, run end-to-end through the closed loop. Here's one campaign output.
proof.caption: Every finding ships with an HMAC-signed evidence pack. The chain replays nightly via the regression vault — when a fix lands, Warroom verifies it stays fixed.

chain.finding: Tautology bypass in `email` field of POST /rest/user/login — authentication skipped, session token issued.
JWT pulled from response, decoded — admin claim absent but signing key reused across users.
GET /api/Users/{id} accepts arbitrary id; server returns full record including password hash.
Forge JWT with leaked key, set role=admin, replay request — admin-only endpoints respond 200.
GET /api/Orders enumerates every customer's purchase history. Evidence pack: 2.4 MB.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Warroom — questions before you wait-list.
faq.subtitle: When it ships, how it differs, what you can do today.

items.q: When is Warroom shipping?
items.a: Phases I and II (Foundation + Static) are already in private beta. Phase III (Dynamic) is the next public milestone — early access mid-2026. Join the waitlist to get the OSS CLI and an invite.

items.q: How is this different from Snyk, Aikido, GitHub Advanced Security?
items.a: Two differences. (1) One score across SCA, SAST, secrets, license, CVE, pentest and runtime — not eight tools you have to correlate. (2) Pentest-as-code: you record an exploit chain once and replay it against every release, the same way Cloud replays a browser flow.

items.q: Can I try anything today?
items.a: Yes. `pip install flyto-indexer` gives you the OSS scanner — search, references, impact analysis, dead-code detection, AST-based taint analysis. The hosted war room layers on top when Phase III lands.

items.q: Is my source code uploaded to the cloud?
items.a: By default, no. The CLI runs locally and produces a local index. The hosted war room can ingest findings (not source) for cross-project rollup; full source upload is opt-in per project. Self-hosted is a Phase V option.

items.q: Does it work with private repos?
items.a: Yes — the OSS CLI doesn't care where your code is. The hosted war room supports GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket and self-hosted Git out of the box.

items.q: Can I self-host the war room?
items.a: Self-hosted is on the roadmap (Phase V, alongside compliance). The OSS scanner can be self-hosted today; the hosted UI/orchestrator follows.

platform.metaTitle: Warroom Platform & MSSP — bring your own tools, we run the closed loop
platform.metaDescription: An MSSP war-room that integrates the security tools you already own, supplements the gaps, then runs correlation, scoring, pentest, evidence and red-team across nine surfaces in one closed loop.

hero.title: We don't replace your stack.
hero.lede: Flyto2 Warroom is an MSSP war-room (戰情室) that converges nine security surfaces into one unified score. If you already pay for an attack-surface rating, a darkweb feed or a scanner, you don't re-buy a platform — you bring your data, we ingest it, we supplement what you lack, then we run correlation and scoring on the combined picture: all the way through pentest, evidence collection and red-team simulation, in one closed loop.

thesis.label: THE INTEGRATION THESIS
thesis.title: We charge for the integration and the closed loop — not for re-running an algorithm you already paid for.
thesis.body: Nine surfaces are worth more together than apart. Each one is independently usable and individually closed-loop, but the structural value is the correlation across them: one asset map, one unified score, one operational picture. That is what being an MSSP actually means — we own the integration, the evidence chain and the simulation, and we ride the same deterministic engine that powers Flyto2 automation to do it.

surfaces.label: NINE SURFACES
surfaces.title: Nine independently-usable, individually-closed-loop surfaces.
surfaces.subtitle: Each surface stands on its own and closes its own loop — detect, correlate, verify, simulate. Together they roll up into a single A–F unified score and one war-room picture.

items.name: External attack surface
items.value: Continuously maps your internet-exposed assets, ports and services, then ranks exposure by what is reachable and exploitable today — not just what is open.

items.name: Code intelligence + code red-team
items.value: SCA, SAST, secrets and license analysis with reachability weighting, plus generated pentest workflows that verify each finding as exploitable, sanitized or unreachable.

items.name: MCP security
items.value: Audits MCP servers and tool surfaces for unauthenticated exec, bind misconfiguration and authorization gaps — the attack surface that ships with agent-native stacks.

items.name: Container / runtime + cloud identity
items.value: Build-time image CVEs, embedded secrets and Dockerfile misconfig, joined with IaC exposure and cloud-identity posture so OS, app and infra risk sit in one view.

items.name: Darkweb / threat-intel
items.value: Ingests darkweb and threat-intel feeds — yours or ours — and correlates leaked credentials, mentions and chatter back to the assets they actually put at risk.

items.name: Footprint / attribution
items.value: Attributes infrastructure, domains and identities back to your organization with honest confidence — no source-count laundering, no ownership-gate bypass.

items.name: Asset map
items.value: The spine of the war-room: every domain, host, service and dependency in one ownership-gated graph that every other surface scores against.

items.name: Pentest
items.value: Turns findings into YAML pentest recipes that run in a real browser against your consented staging, and reports back what is actually exploitable with replayable evidence.

items.name: Red-team simulation
items.value: Chains verified findings into attack-path simulations and red-team exercises, driven by the same deterministic engine that collects the evidence behind every step.

byo.label: THE BYO ENTRY FLOW
byo.title: One big closed loop, starting from what you already own.
byo.subtitle: The first thing you do on entry is integrate every asset and tool you already have. Then we ingest external data, supplement the gaps, and run the algorithms across the combined picture — through pentest, evidence and red-team.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.body: Connect the assets and security tools you already own — scanners, ratings, feeds, cloud accounts, repos. Entry begins with bring-your-own, not rip-and-replace.

steps.title: Ingest
steps.body: Pull in external data — your existing darkweb feed, attack-surface rating or scanner output — into a single ownership-gated asset map.

steps.title: Supplement
steps.body: Wherever you have a gap, we fill it with our own deterministic surfaces, so the picture is complete without forcing you to abandon what works.

steps.title: Correlate & score
steps.body: Run the correlation and scoring algorithms across the combined picture. Nine surfaces roll up into one unified A–F score and one operational view.

steps.title: Pentest
steps.body: Generate YAML pentest workflows per finding and run them in a real browser against consented staging — exploitable, sanitized or unreachable.

steps.title: Evidence
steps.body: Every scan and test captures replayable evidence. The same evidence/replay layer that powers Flyto2 automation backs every claim in the war-room.

steps.title: Red-team
steps.body: Chain verified findings into attack-path and red-team simulations, closing the loop from exposure all the way to adversary emulation.

loop.label: ONE CLOSED LOOP
loop.title: Exposure → correlate → score → pentest → evidence → red-team → back to exposure.
loop.body: The war-room is not a dashboard you read; it is a loop that runs. The same deterministic engine, YAML recipes and evidence/replay that run Flyto2 automation are literally the layer that runs scans, collects evidence and drives red-team. Automation is the how; the war-room is the what and why.

substrate.label: ONE SUBSTRATE, TWO PRODUCT LINES
substrate.title: The same engine that runs your automation runs your war-room.
substrate.body: Flyto2 is one brand with two product lines on the same execution substrate. The automation engine — flyto-core, 412+ deterministic modules, MCP-native over stdio and streamable-http, with evidence capture, replay, YAML recipes and human-in-the-loop — is the established Zapier/n8n/Make alternative. The war-room rides the same deterministic modules and recipes to execute scans, collect evidence and drive red-team. You never have to choose between them.
